semantic_correction.stem: A client has a mature arteriovenous fistula for hemodialysis. Which statement shows correct understanding of access protection?

options.A: I will avoid blood pressure checks and blood draws on the access arm and check regularly for the usual thrill and infection changes.
options.B: I can use the access arm for blood pressure checks once the fistula has matured and is working well.
options.C: I should leave access checks to dialysis staff and avoid monitoring the fistula between treatments.
options.D: If the usual thrill disappears, I can wait until my next dialysis session as long as the arm is not painful.

semantic_correction.rationale: Current National Kidney Foundation guidance instructs clients with a hemodialysis fistula or graft not to allow blood pressure measurement or blood draws on the access arm. Clients should check the access routinely for the normal vibration or thrill and contact the dialysis team promptly if the thrill is absent or changes. NIDDK guidance also recommends daily inspection of the access for signs of infection such as warmth or redness. Therefore option A best reflects access protection and self-monitoring.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Protect an arteriovenous fistula by avoiding blood pressure measurement and blood draws on the access arm and by monitoring the usual thrill and signs of infection.

semantic_correction.source_locator: NKF Caring for Your Access — do not allow blood pressure measurement or blood draws on the access arm; call the dialysis team at once if the thrill/bruit is absent or different. audit_findings_append.finding: The original answer was uniquely longest and one distractor used absolute wording. The revised item tests access-arm protection and patient self-monitoring with balanced alternatives.

option_audit.A: Correct. It combines the directly recommended access-arm protections with routine thrill and infection monitoring.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Blood pressure cuffs should not be used on the access arm even after the fistula matures.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Clients are taught to check the access between treatments rather than relying solely on dialysis staff.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Loss or change of the usual thrill requires prompt contact with the dialysis team.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone combines the current access-protection and self-monitoring recommendations without delaying response to dysfunction.
cueing_check: All four choices are client statements about AV-fistula care of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
